violation_type.title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - Licensed Child Care Home (26 TAC §747.1801)
violation_type.short_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - Licensed Child Care Home
violation_type.typical_finding: A total of one caregiver and ten children were observed inside the licensed childcare home. The maximum children allowed is seven children based on their age group. The licensed childcare home is out of ratio by three children.

finding_variants.text: A total of one caregiver and ten children were observed inside the licensed childcare home. The maximum children allowed is seven children based on their age group. The licensed childcare home is out of ratio by three children.
There were 11 children observed in the home, including 2 infants.  The operation was observed to be out of child/caregiver ratio for one caregiver.

During this inspection, the primary caregiver was the only caregiver present as her husband was not there. There were 2 infants and 8 children ages 18 months to 3yo, for a total of 10 children. The caregiver corrected this by having 3 children between the ages of 18mo-3yo be picked up by parents. She then came into compliance with 2 infants and 5 children ages 18mo-3yo.

A caregiver was alone at the home with 14 children. Ages of the children were as follows: 4 months, 14 months, 20 months, 22 months, 2 years, 2 years, 2 years, 3 years, 3 years, 4 years, 4 years, 4 years, 4 years, and 5 years.     This was corrected at inspection when another caregiver arrived at the home and 2 children ages 4 months and 2 years of age were sent home, bringing the home into ratio.
Permit holder was over ratio based on ages of children.

The operation was out of ratio and had more kids than they should have had based on the ages of the children in care. There were eleven children in care with one caregiver. There were three infants, seven children between 18 months and three years old, and one child 4 years old and up.
